**From spectral measurements to vegetation trait retrieval**

In-person training course **“Advanced Applications of Open Satellite Data”**, organised by the International Italo-Latin American Organization (IILA) in collaboration with the Italian Space Agency (ASI). Córdoba, Argentina | **30 November–2 December 2026**.

[![RTM-Suite](https://img.shields.io/badge/Framework-RTM--Suite-287D46)](https://rtm-suite.wur.nl/) [![R](https://img.shields.io/badge/Language-R-276DC3)](https://www.r-project.org/) [![ToolsRTM](https://img.shields.io/badge/Package-ToolsRTM-287D46)](https://rtm-suite.wur.nl/toolsrtm/)

## Overview

This repository provides hands-on training materials for vegetation remote sensing, radiative transfer modelling (RTM), spectral sensitivity analysis and plant trait retrieval using R and RTM-Suite.

The practical session combines physically based simulations with field hyperspectral observations and machine learning. Participants progress from understanding soil, leaf and canopy optical properties to retrieving vegetation traits from measured reflectance spectra.

## Learning objectives

- Understand how soil, leaf and canopy properties influence vegetation reflectance.
- Perform forward simulations using PROSPECT and fourSAIL (PROSAIL).
- Generate synthetic look-up tables (LUTs).
- Explore individual trait effects and global spectral sensitivity.
- Convolve hyperspectral simulations to satellite sensor spectral bands.
- Investigate relationships between spectral indices and measured nitrogen.
- Compare classical LUT inversion and Random Forest retrieval approaches.

## Practical exercises

| Exercise | Topic | Duration |
|:--|:--|--:|
| 01 | [From soil and leaf to canopy reflectance](Exercises/01-Explore-Canopy.Rmd) | 20 min |
| 02 | [Trait sensitivity and a simulation LUT](Exercises/02-Trait-Sensitivity.Rmd) | 20 min |
| 03 | [Field spectra and vegetation trait inversion](Exercises/03-Field-Spectra-and-Trait-Inversion.Rmd) | 30 min |
| | **Total** | **70 min** |

### Exercise 1 — Explore canopy reflectance

Explore the RTM-Suite interactive simulator, generate a small LUT, compare measured and simulated soil spectra, and investigate how leaf chlorophyll content (Cab) and leaf area index (LAI) influence canopy reflectance.

### Exercise 2 — Trait sensitivity

Perform controlled trait sweeps, simulate a LUT, convolve hyperspectral reflectance to satellite spectral bands and investigate global spectral sensitivity when multiple model inputs vary together.

### Exercise 3 — Field spectra and vegetation trait inversion

Analyse hyperspectral measurements from 40 plots in a grazed fen meadow in the Achterhoek, the Netherlands. Explore nitrogen-related spectral indices, generate a 500-row PROSAIL LUT, compare classical inversion cost functions and train Random Forest models to retrieve:

- **Cab:** leaf chlorophyll content.
- **LAI:** leaf area index.
- **EWT:** equivalent water thickness.

Apply the inversion models to field spectra and explore relationships between retrieved traits, measured nitrogen and biomass.

## Conceptual workflow

```text
Soil, leaf and canopy properties
              |
              v
      PROSAIL forward model
              |
              v
   Synthetic spectra and LUTs
              |
              v
 Spectral sensitivity and sensor convolution
              |
              v
   Classical / Random Forest inversion <--- Field spectra
              |
              v
     Vegetation trait retrieval
              |
              v
 Relationships with nitrogen and biomass
```

## Getting started

Use this order the first time you work with the course:

1. Install **R 4.5.1 or newer** from [CRAN](https://cran.r-project.org/) and [RStudio Desktop](https://posit.co/download/rstudio-desktop/). The exercises were checked with R 4.5.1.
2. Get the course from the [GitHub repository](https://github.com/CCGCAM/IILA-Remote-Sensing-Course): select **Code > Download ZIP**, or clone it with Git. Keep all folders together when extracting the ZIP.
3. Open the `.Rproj` file in the repository's top folder. This sets the working directory so the relative file paths work.
4. In the RStudio Console, run the package installer **once**:

   ```r
   source("install_packages.R")
   ```

   An internet connection is needed while packages and ToolsRTM are installed. Wait for the `Ready` message before continuing.
5. Read `00-Setup_practical.html`. Then open `Exercises/01-Explore-Canopy.Rmd` in RStudio and run its chunks from top to bottom. Start the Shiny simulator from its marked chunk or run `source("run_app.R")` in the Console. Stop the app before continuing with the code chunks.
6. Continue with Exercises 2 and 3, running chunks in order and answering each blue question box. The `_practical.html` files are for reading; use the `.Rmd` files to run or change code.

To reinstall after an incomplete installation, restart RStudio and run `source("install_packages.R")` again from the project root. You do not need to run `render_exercises.R` as a participant; it is for rebuilding the HTML handouts.

### Before the class

Complete the download, R/RStudio installation and package installation before arriving. Open `00-Setup_practical.html` and the three `_practical.html` exercise pages in a web browser to read the instructions and explore their interactive plots. HTML is the preparation and reference material; it does not execute R code. To run the exercises, open the matching `.Rmd` file in RStudio and run each chunk in order. If possible, run `source("run_app.R")` once before class and confirm that the local simulator opens.

The interactive simulator runs locally in RStudio through the Shiny app included in this repository. It does not run as part of the static HTML pages.
